observation_reviews.rationale: The fix is supported. Point (a): I read 10 of the 75 rows on the page across 8 quarters (Chase 2023-12-31 and 2024-06-30, Hellers BKBM and BBSY 2024-12-31, Plaskolite 2025-06-30, PlentyMarkets 2025-09-30, New Gen and V Global 2026-03-31, Gulf Winds 2026-06-30, Hellers 2026-03-31). Each publishes basis_spread = cash + PIK, pik_rate = the printed PIK and interest_rate = the printed coupon (all_in), with interest_rate_cash = coupon - PIK. The cash leg is not understated: coupon - (cash + PIK) gives SOFR 5.33 to 5.35 in 2023-2024, 4.2 to 4.3 in 2025 and 3.6 to 3.9 in 2026; read as a cash coupon, the base would be 6.85 (Chase 2023-12-31) or 7.15 (Hellers BBSY). Rejected on the detection decision. As written, the suggested_check computes interest_rate - basis_spread - pik_rate. On a wrong row (spread = cash A) that equals the benchmark, so it does not fire. On a corrected row (spread = A + B) it equals benchmark - PIK. The check therefore flags the fixed rows and passes the defect. The working form is interest_rate - basis_spread compared with the benchmark: a residual of about +pik_rate means the spread holds only the cash part. Amend suggested_check before it is proposed.
